convoLines.text: "What's something you're good at that nobody here knows about?"
"Noted. Filing that under 'extremely useful.' The village needs that."
"I can do trapping. Not well — well enough that nobody's died from it yet. That's my whole résumé now: nobody's died from it yet. Just... be straight with me."
"Still on what you're good at."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? That's all."
"Good question." "Gabriela always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Alright. Catch you later."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Is there someone here you don't trust? Be honest."
Their eyes flick, just for a second, toward the fire. "Noted. I'll watch too."
"I don't distrust anyone exactly — I just haven't finished trusting most of them yet. There's a difference. A slow one."
"Still on who you don't trust."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Let's move."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Gabriela is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"What's the kindest thing someone's done for you out here? Easy."
"That's the good stuff. Quiet generosity. It's holding this whole thing together."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"Someone saved me the last of the stew once. Didn't say anything, just put the bowl down and walked off. I think about that bowl more than I think about the monsters."
"Don't care what it is. Care what it does. It gives powers for doing things — so we do things. Theory's for people with full bellies."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on the big questions."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Goldenrod — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Go on, then. I'll be thinking good thoughts at you."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Have you — sorry. I keep thinking about them."
Terrence has an edge today — something curdled.
"There's still the matter of the murder of Nadia. Nobody's settled it."
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You follow the food, the gifts, the sudden friendliness. Nothing you can prove — yet. Dig again; the trail is still warm.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
Counted.
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
"Can we talk?" Oscar glances around first. "People are saying things. About you. Is any of it true?"
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Oscar grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Oscar is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"My cut needs a second pair of hands. Will you help me clean it?"
"Every day it's angrier. I need it cleaned before it turns — I can't work a wound like this. Wrap it tight when you're done."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"

"Good question." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Have you heard what they're calling Drum-Belly? Terrence is pushing 'Big Big'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"All right. I wanted to ask rather than assume."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Never mind this wound — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took Boris — The Pit, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
They give you the benefit of the doubt. This time.
"I show up. That's my part."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on what's been happening."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Oscar is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I tell you something? Before the scattering, I said something cruel. I think about it every day."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what they confided."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
You show them American Persimmon — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Don't tell anyone I told you. What's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "The Pit. They just... took Boris. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"Rest when you can. We'll talk again soon."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.

lines: d6: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d6: 🕯️ Gabriela Ramos is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d6: What Gabriela kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d6: Roman picks up the journal. Their hands shake. Then they open it, and keep writing.
d6: 📖 LEARNED: Scrounger (Level 1). Ruin looting finds +1 item.
d6: 📖 LEARNED: Herbal Medicine (Level 1). Willow bark = aspirin. Yarrow stops bleeding. Plantain draws out infection. The pharmacy is outside.
d6: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d6: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Gabriela Ramos, 6 days. The mantle passes to Roman Pavlov.
d6: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Roman Pavlov, 28 — a hotel housekeeper. His hands know different work now: Green Whisper.
d6: The fire knew Roman — solid ground, earned at this fire.

lastSay: d31: — DAY 31 DAWN — The world wakes. Animals are active.
d31: 🎁 You find a small bundle tucked where you'll find it. No one saw it left there.
d31: "They're sending Vex after you tomorrow. He's bored. Be somewhere else."
d31: (401 kcal of dried meat and clean water. Nothing traceable.)
d31: Dawn. You wake rested. (+0 health, energy restored. By the fire. Good enough.)
